chunks: Aḥmad ibn Idrīs narrated to me, he said: Aḥmad ibn Abī Zāhir narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusain al-Zayyāt from Ḥusain ibn ‘Imrān from ‘Imrān, who said: I asked Abī al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him)
Should I shorten the prayer in the Sacred Mosque or complete it? He said: If you shorten it, you may; but if you complete it, it is better, and increasing in goodness is better.
ai.seo_question: Should I shorten or complete my prayers when visiting the Kaaba?
ai.summary: Imam al-Kāżim (peace be upon him) clarifies that while shortening the prayer (qasr) is valid in the Sacred Mosque, completing it (tamm) is superior as it yields greater reward. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that voluntary acts of worship performed with full devotion in sacred spaces are meritorious, even when the default legal ruling permits brevity. The narration underscores the spiritual value of intention and completeness in ritual practice within the holiest sites.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 10. Aḥmad ibn Idrīs narrated to me from Aḥmad ibn Abī Zāhir, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain Al-Zayyāt, from Ḥusain ibn ‘Imrān, from ‘Imrān, who said: I asked Abal Ḥasan (Imam Kāżim (a.s.)),

“Should I establish prayers in Taqsīr or in full form when I am in Masjid Al-Ḥarām?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “You can choose to pray in Taqsīr but it is better if you pray in full form because doing more good deeds is always a blessing.”
